finding_dispositions.note: interpretations.md Reading 3 difficulty rewritten. It quotes Matthew 22:15 (Clementine 'consilium inierunt', Douay 'consulted among themselves') as silent on whether the purpose was known. The objection is built from Jerome's 'Prima virtus est respondentis' (PL 26 col. 163) and from Chrysostom's own note that they asked 'in the presence of the multitude' (Hom. 70.1, NPNF 1/10 lines 39512-39517); it says Chrysostom draws only their 'folly' from the crowd. Chrysostom's answer is quoted from lines 39563-39568: respectful, true words, 'being God' not deceived, so the rebuke is not conjecture. scope.md 3.1 gives that reasoning with loci. It bounds 'complete and manifest' (39557-39560) and states that no study may say the consultation was open. The outcome line, the section 7 row and the NPNF binding context agree.
